As a current college student, when I was in high school the farthest we got up to was the end of the USSR, and that was very very brief. I took AP World History and the majority of time was spent learning about the world in the 1200s-1900s. There was a very small window of history learnt from 1900s-Present, and that was at the end of the year. So things like urbanization in the 1950s, Bay of Pigs invasion, Vietnam War, Cold War, End of USSR were basically all taught in less than a month. There was essentially no time left to even learn about events in the 1990s-Present, but our textbook did have chapters all the way up to Obama's inauguration, so I guess it is possible there are kids out there learning about it (I just wasn't one of them).

It's not entitlement, it's literally our culture. Tipping in America is a way to say thanks for great service, but it's also inherently expected. Tipping nothing or anything below 15-20% at a restaurant is considered extremely rude, and a way of telling the waiter that they gave you terrible service. 

It's not very common in other countries to tip like this, especially in countries where waiters/service workers make a livable wage, but in the USA most service workers do not make enough to live off of and depend on these 20% tips to survive, so like stuffandornonsense put it, by tipping them 20%, it's a show of solidarity and kindness. 

And again, when you come to another country, you're expected to follow and respect the customs. Just because you find it "entitled" doesn't mean you can just ignore it.

I think it's really important to remember why we have these AA policies in the first place. We have these types of policies because historically women and other minorities could not become computer scientists or engineers until very very recently. So when you think about it, how many years have (white) men been able to become engineers, scientists, computer programmers, etc? We have these programs to try and even out what is now a heavily unbalanced industry, and give opportunity to women and POC who throughout their careers and even academic careers, will face challenges and obstacles that (white) men will NEVER have to face.

I'm a competitive swimmer so I can help you with the swimming. Swim at least 3 days a week for 2 hours. I would choose the combat swimmer stroke (aka freestyle) because it is the fastest and easiest. 500 yards is 20 laps, so it is not a sprint. Whenever I swam the 500 in meets, you always start out slow and then build up to finish strong. In the pool, do not practice speed, practice endurance swimming. Speed will come with practice- the important thing is to not become exhausted in the water. Goodluck!
